summary: Our project, "They Will Not Be Forgotten", is an interactive storytelling website that introduces school-age space enthusiasts to the NASA hardware left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Twelve spacecraft, including the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity and Voyager 1, are shown on a clickable map with a status badge such as Retired, Lost contact or Still traveling. Each spacecraft has its own story page, written in its own voice, so young learners meet these machines as characters instead of cold facts. Next to each story, a gallery shows real NASA photos of the spacecraft and images it captured, loaded live from the NASA Image and Video Library with credits and links to the originals. The site works in English and Turkish. These missions gave us huge scientific discoveries, yet their stories are rarely told to young people. By turning science into emotion and curiosity, we hope to inspire the next generation of explorers.
details: What it does: Our website, "Abandoned but Not Forgotten", tells the stories of 12 NASA spacecraft left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Users explore a map, choose a spacecraft and click "Go to its story". Each story page has a short first-person story (for example, "Hi, I'm Opportunity...") and an image gallery with two parts: photos of the spacecraft itself and images taken by it. A status badge (Retired, Lost contact, Still traveling) shows where each mission stands today. Benefits and intended impact: The project helps school-age learners connect emotionally with space exploration. Stories are easier to remember than lists of facts. Teachers and parents can use the site as a simple starting point for lessons about the Moon, Mars and the outer solar system. The English and Turkish language option makes it accessible to more students. Tools and technology: We built the website with Lovable, an AI web app builder that uses React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS. All spacecraft images are loaded from the NASA Image and Video Library API. We used Claude, an AI assistant, to write prompts and draft the spacecraft stories, which our team reviewed. How it is creative: Instead of a standard fact page, every spacecraft speaks as a character. The map and the status badges turn a mission archive into an emotional journey, and real NASA images are loaded automatically so the gallery stays authentic. Factors our team considered: We kept the language simple, short and friendly for school-age readers. We checked facts against NASA mission information. Every image shows "Credit: NASA" and links to its original page. All stories and image search terms are stored in data files, so new spacecraft can be added easily. We did not use any NASA logos or mission identifiers in our design.
